sa: संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
tr: saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi
en: Krishna, you praise the renunciation of action, and then again its disciplined practice. Tell me decisively which one of the two is better.
speaker: Arjuna said

en: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good, but of the two, the yoga of action is better than renouncing action.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति।
tr: jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati
en: Know as a true renunciate the one who neither hates nor craves. Free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed, such a person is easily set free from bondage.
Children, not the wise, speak of Sankhya and Yoga as different. Whoever is truly established in even one of them gains the fruit of both.

sa: एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
tr: ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
en: The state reached by the followers of Sankhya is reached by the yogis too. Whoever sees Sankhya and Yoga as one truly sees.
But renunciation, mighty-armed, is hard to attain without yoga. The sage disciplined in yoga reaches Brahman before long.
Disciplined in yoga, pure in heart, master of self and senses, whose self has become the self of all beings: such a person is not stained even while acting.
"I do nothing at all," thinks the disciplined one who knows the truth, while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing,
speaking, letting go, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, holding firmly that it is only the senses moving among their objects.

sa: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।
tr: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
en: Whoever acts offering every action to Brahman, letting go of attachment, is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
Yogis act with body, mind and intellect, even with the senses alone, letting go of attachment, to purify the self.
The disciplined one, giving up the fruit of action, reaches lasting peace; the undisciplined, driven by desire and attached to the fruit, is bound.

sa: नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥
tr: navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan
en: Renouncing all actions with the mind, the self-controlled embodied one rests happily in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing action.

sa: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः।
tr: na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ
en: The Lord does not create agency or actions for the world, nor the link between action and its fruit; it is one's own nature that carries these on.

sa: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।
tr: nādatte kasyacitpāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ
en: The all-pervading one takes on no one's sin or merit. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and so beings are deluded.
But for those whose ignorance is destroyed by knowledge of the Self, that knowledge, like the sun, lights up the Supreme.
Minds fixed on That, their self one with That, established in That and devoted to That, their impurities shaken off by knowledge, they go where there is no return.

sa: शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
tr: śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ
en: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and one who eats dogs.

sa: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
tr: ihaiva tairjitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmādbrahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
en: Even here, birth and death are conquered by those whose minds rest in equality. Brahman is flawless and the same in all, so they rest in Brahman.
Not elated at getting what is pleasant, not shaken at getting what is unpleasant, steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman rests in Brahman.
Unattached to outer contacts, one finds the happiness that is in the Self; joined to Brahman through yoga, one enjoys a happiness that never ends.

sa: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
tr: ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ
en: Pleasures born of contact are wombs of sorrow; they have a beginning and an end, son of Kunti. The wise do not delight in them.

sa: कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
tr: kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ
en: Whoever, here, before leaving the body, can withstand the surge of desire and anger is disciplined; that person is happy.
Whoever is happy within, delights within and is lit from within, that yogi, one with Brahman, reaches the peace of Brahman (brahma-nirvana).
Sages whose impurities are worn away, whose doubts are cut, who are self-controlled and delight in the good of all beings, attain the peace of Brahman.
For ascetics free from desire and anger, minds controlled, who know the Self, the peace of Brahman is near on every side.
Shutting out outer contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, making the in-breath and out-breath even as they move within the nostrils,

sa: विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
tr: vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
en: senses, mind and intellect controlled, intent on freedom, with desire, fear and anger gone: that sage is free forever.
Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all the worlds and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
